study_identification_part.si4_title: Individual deviations from normative models of brain structure in a large cross-sectional schizophrenia cohort

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: This study aimed to map individual deviations from normative ranges of brain structure in schizophrenia patients and evaluate if these deviations align with group-average pathology maps. It also explored genetic and clinical drivers of such deviations.

rci9_site_effect_handling.detail: Multiple detailed methods for handling site effects are described, including pre-acquisition calibration, post-acquisition harmonization for dMRI, and inclusion of site as a covariate in the normative model. Prior inter-site calibration using a phantom and a traveling individual; retrospective harmonization for diffusion-weighted images using a robust nonlinear mapping procedure (reference site Brisbane, age and sex-matched healthy controls for other sites, based on rotation invariant spherical harmonics); acquisition site included as a nuisance confound/covariate ($C_i$) in quantile regression model; harmonization not performed for structural MRI as CT maps were consistent across sites.
rci9_site_effect_handling.supporting_text: An individual traveled to all /uniFB01 ve sites and was scanned at each site to quantify gross inter-site differences. A Siemens MRI phantom was also scanned at each site to enable intersite calibration. In addition, in this study, the diffusionweighted images were retrospectively harmonized to alleviate possible nonlinear site-related differences. We followed a robust harmonization procedure developed in our previous work [29]. Speci /uniFB01 cally, a reference site was selected (Brisbane), with age and sex-matched healthy controls from each remaining site (Supplementary Table 1). These healthy control subsets were used to compute a nonlinear mapping of the diffusion MRI signals between the reference site and each remaining target site, based on features of rotation invariant spherical harmonics [29]. This mapping was then used to update the diffusion-weighted images for each remaining individual. Ci encapsulates nuisance confounds, including acquisition site. Second, while data harmonization was performed to minimize inter-site differences in FA, deviation maps were not reproduced for the two smallest sites (Newcastle, Perth). In contrast, deviation maps in CT were consistent between virtually all sites, and thus harmonization was not performed on the structural MRI images.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Pearson correlation for AAI with polygenic risk score (PRS) and cognitive/symptom dimensions; Canonical Correlation Analysis (CCA) with permutation testing (5000 permutations) and familywise error rate control for multivariate associations between deviation scores and PRS/cognitive-symptom dimensions; Two-sample t-tests with permutation testing (5000 permutations) and False Discovery Rate (FDR) control at 5% for individual DIP items and deviation scores; Pearson correlation for AAI (CT/FA) with current IQ.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Schizophrenia-related brain structural changes are highly heterogeneous across individuals, making group-consensus pathological maps unrepresentative of most individual patients, but normative modeling can help parse this heterogeneity.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Group-level analyses showed widespread reductions in FA and CT in schizophrenia patients, affecting 83% of white matter tracts and 88% of cortical regions. However, individually, no more than 17-18% of patients deviated from the normative range for any single tract or region. Despite this, 79% of patients exhibited infra-normal deviations in at least one locus (compared to 59 ± 2% of healthy individuals, p < 0.001), while 46% showed supra-normal deviations (compared to 61 ± 3% of healthy individuals, p < 0.001), indicating high individual heterogeneity in deviation loci. Higher polygenic risk for schizophrenia was associated with a greater number of regions with infra-normal CT deviations (r = -0.17, p = 0.006). Multivariate analyses revealed a significant association between PRS and deviation scores (CCA r = 0.69, p = 0.044) and a marginally significant association between symptom/cognition dimensions and deviation scores (CCA r = 0.75, p = 0.048).

caa10_key_limitations.answer: MRI data noise and artifacts; dMRI harmonization issues at smaller sites; subjective definition of normative ranges (5-95% percentiles); smaller normative sample size; individual variation in medication status, age of onset, and illness duration; potential for alternative normative modeling techniques.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: First, MRI data are inherently noisy and individual measurements are particularly susceptible to the effects of noise and imaging artifacts. Some individual deviations could have been spurious and owing to noise... Second, while data harmonization was performed to minimize inter-site differences in FA, deviation maps were not reproduced for the two smallest sites (Newcastle, Perth)... Third, normative ranges were operationalized subjectively (5 -95% percentiles)... Fourth, individual variation in medication status, age of onset, and illness duration could potentially contribute to heterogeneity. Fifth, while quantile regression is robust... alternative normative modeling techniques... should be considered...

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Individual deviation maps can identify personalized targets for neural stimulation therapies, enable patient-centered approaches to antipsychotic drug selection, and delineate putative subtypes.
